mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% for three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and depressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in the housing market (HOUST) signals weakening consumer demand offset by housing strength, resulting in flat to slightly positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > 0% MoM for 2 consecutive months
regime_hint: late-cycle consumption slowdown with housing resilience
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 4% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month - 0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in the federal funds rate of more than 0.75 percentage points, combined with a concurrent rise in CPIAUCSL above 3%, signals aggressive monetary tightening and heightened inflation risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS change > 0.75% AND CPIAUCSL change > 3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (proxied by RSAFS growth > 1% for three consecutive months) during a period of stable employment (UNRATE change near zero) signals elevated precautionary savings and lower marginal propensity to consume, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > 1% for 3 consecutive months AND UNRATE change within -0.1 to +0.1% for same 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) acceleration above 0.5% for two consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports corporate earnings and justifies higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below 900K units for four consecutive months signals a prolonged housing downturn, which reduces construction-related earnings and drags on consumer spending, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
